title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with a synthetic likeness. Someone used an AI deepfake on a WhatsApp video call to appear as a sitting chief minister, then layered ordinary fraud on top of it: a person posing as a manager, a letter claiming funds had been allotted, and a second person claiming to be a CBI officer. The deepfake did the work of establishing authority at the start, and the rest of the scheme converted that authority into payments. The failure sits at the point where a public figure's face and voice can be produced on a consumer messaging app with nothing in the call itself to indicate the likeness was generated.

Nothing in the call or in the documents that followed let the recipient confirm any of the identities being claimed. The allotment letter and the identity proof were supplied by the same people demanding money, so the only check available was to reach the offices being named through a separate channel. No such check occurred before the payments were made, and the fraud ended only when the recipient refused a further demand.

What is not established is who made the deepfake, whether the person on the video call was the same person who posed as the manager or the CBI officer, and whether any of the claimed allotment existed. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act, which is a complaint and not a finding.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29 year old Bengaluru security guard, Ratikanta Giri, from Odisha, received a WhatsApp video call on September 9. The caller used an AI deepfake to appear as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay and offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid. A person posing as a manager said Rs 5 lakh was allotted and asked for fees. Giri first paid Rs 5,000, then Rs 18,000, and later paid more after someone claiming to be a CBI officer demanded over Rs 50,000. His total loss was over Rs 1.04 lakh.

When the fraudsters asked for another Rs 50,000, Giri refused and realized he had been cheated. He contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then approached Byappanahalli police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act. The article says this is the first such case reported in the city. Fraudsters had sent him a letter claiming Rs 5 lakh was allotted and identity proof said to belong to a CBI officer. Police urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on such claims.
